scope: Eight bounded cases through four shell aliases compare native GNU and Rboxc: ordinary self-directed USR1, restart from USR1, return from USR1/INT within a function, and DEBUG/ERR/RETURN/INT handlers that reset themselves before executing a private plain script. All candidate process summaries must be complete and clean; native findings are preserved.

results.name: bash:user-signal-normal
args: trap 'printf signal\n' USR1; kill -s USR1 $$; printf 'after:%s\n' "$?"

results.name: bash:user-signal-restart
args: trap 'exec ./plain user-signal' USR1; kill -s USR1 $$; printf unreachable

results.name: bash:user-signal-return
args: trap 'return 7' USR1; f(){ kill -s USR1 $$; printf unreachable; }; f; printf 'returned:%s\n' "$?"

results.name: bash:interrupt-return
args: trap 'return 9' INT; f(){ kill -s INT $$; printf unreachable; }; f; printf 'returned:%s\n' "$?"

results.name: bash:error-reset-restart
args: trap 'trap - ERR; exec ./plain reset-error' ERR; false

results.name: bash:return-reset-restart
args: set -T; trap 'trap - RETURN; exec ./plain reset-return' RETURN; f(){ :; }; f

results.name: bash:interrupt-reset-restart
args: trap 'trap - INT; exec ./plain reset-interrupt' INT; kill -s INT $$
